title: 902: The Missing Minutes
summary_zh: 本期围绕人生的“记忆空白与未解之谜”展开：当我们苦寻多年终于获知真相，或某天一切困惑突然得到解答时，我们会走向何处？代班主持人 Aviva DeKornfeld 在 Prologue 中切入温哥华机场酒吧的卧底现场，身藏录音器的 Vienna Luke 等待十余年未见的姐夫 Justin，追问二十岁那晚失落的记忆。Act One 呈现了这场惊心动魄的对峙：Vienna 冷静套出姐夫下药与偷拍的罪证，虽将其送入监狱、解开十四年心结，却未能唤回偏袒丈夫的大姐 Sunny。Act Two 由 Miranda July 朗读短篇小说，从“已知的未知”转向“未知的未知”：主人公突然被告知过往苦难只是一场测试，所有人都在野餐会上等着爱她，但她却逃回浴缸与床榻，在熟悉而遗憾的孤独中安然入睡。
key_takeaways_zh: Prologue（主持人 Aviva DeKornfeld）：在温哥华机场酒店酒吧的警方卧底现场，身藏两个隐秘录音器的 Vienna Luke 等待十年未见的姐夫 Justin 现身，准备揭开困扰她十余年的记忆空白。
Act One: Known Unknowns（记者 Aviva DeKornfeld）：Vienna Luke 在事发十四年后孤身对峙曾给自己下药性侵的姐夫 Justin 并套出全部罪证，最终将其送入联邦监狱并获得精神解脱，却依然未能唤回执迷不悟的大姐 Sunny。
Act Two: Unknown Unknowns（作者与朗读 Miranda July）：一篇超现实短篇小说设想某天主人公突然得知过往人生的所有伤痛与遗憾都只是一场“测试”，但在众人盛大的爱意面前，她却本能地逃回孤独而熟悉的日常悲剧中。

highlights.summary_zh: 温哥华机场酒店酒吧里，Vienna Luke 在手提包和内衣里各藏了一个录音器，在便衣警察的暗中包围下等待十年未见的姐夫 Justin。面对十多年前那晚记忆断片的长期折磨，她终于迎来了当面质问所有真相的时刻。
highlights.quote_en: So what's it like to actually get all the answers you spent so long wondering about? And where's that leave you?

highlights.summary_zh: 故事回溯到十四年前，二十岁的福音派女孩 Vienna 在大姐 Sunny 外出时，听信教会领袖姐夫 Justin“在安全环境体验醉酒”的提议喝下调酒。她很快双腿失去知觉昏迷，醒来时只残留一段姐夫脱下她内裤的离体记忆，而全家为了维持表面和睦选择了沉默。
highlights.quote_en: Oh, do you want to, like, get drunk, to experience what it's like to be drunk in a safe place?

highlights.title_zh: 前同事揭开下药与偷拍
highlights.summary_zh: 事发十二年后，Vienna 决定彻查真相，二姐 Shaughnessy 协助联系了 Justin 兽医诊所的前员工。前员工不仅证实 Justin 曾询问如何给人类下药使其彻底昏迷，还透露诊所电脑里曾发现他与昏迷裸女的自拍照，这促成警方启动正式卧底调查。
highlights.quote_en: And she says, 'I know why you're calling. He drugged your sister.'

highlights.summary_zh: 经过卧底警察的训练，Vienna 带着问题清单在机场酒吧与 Justin 正面交锋。每当 Justin 试图用戒除性瘾学来的心理学术语或“社会物化女性”等空泛借口推卸责任时，Vienna 都异常坚定而敏锐地将对话拉回那晚的具体事实上。
highlights.quote_en: Okay, but you're not actually telling me what happened.

highlights.summary_zh: 在 Vienna 的步步紧逼下，Justin 承认在酒里下药、拍下三十张裸照并在她身上自慰，甚至在谈话尾声顺带供出曾多次在窗外偷拍她。令人震惊的是，他始终用一套自欺欺人的“行为底线”为自己开脱，在一个半小时的对峙中未曾说过一句抱歉。
highlights.quote_en: He's come up with a story he can tell himself so that he's still a good person, because there are lines he drew and rules he set that he stayed on the right side of.

highlights.title_zh: 解开心结与大姐的曲奇
highlights.summary_zh: 对峙结束后，强撑许久的 Vienna 冲进洗手间迎来生理性的情绪释放；这份录音铁证最终将 Justin 送进联邦监狱，也让她彻底摆脱了十四年的精神囚禁。然而大姐 Sunny 始终站在丈夫一边未曾听过录音，Vienna 最终吃掉了大姐托 Justin 捎来的曲奇，心底仍留有一丝期盼。
highlights.quote_en: It's kind of crazy how captive I was to everything that was done to me, the not knowing, and how much it, yeah, dictated so much of my life.

highlights.summary_zh: 第二幕转向生活中那些难以名状的缺失感，作家 Miranda July 朗读了一篇短篇小说。故事中主人公突然收到通知：她通过了测试，过往人生中所有的冷漠老师、混蛋前任与困顿境遇都只是为了检验她有多坚强而演的戏，所有人都在公园野餐会等待拥抱她。
highlights.quote_en: It was all just a test. We were only kidding. Real life is so much better than that.

highlights.title_zh: 逃离完美野餐躲进浴缸
highlights.summary_zh: 身处被所有人无条件深爱的奇幻野餐会中，主人公却借口去查邮政信箱，随后径直开车回家泡进浴缸。她放了全世界鸽子，搞砸了被所有人接纳的唯一机会，却在这场自我制造的遗憾重压下感受到一种近乎体温的踏实感，安然入睡。
highlights.quote_en: As this person climbs into bed, the weight of this tragedy seems to bear down upon this person's chest. And it is a comforting weight, almost human in heft.

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 身上暗藏窃听或录音设备
vocab_notes.note_zh: 源自刑侦与影视俚语（常简作 wear a wire），指卧底或线人在衣物下隐藏麦克风和录音器以秘密取证。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 已知的未知（明确知道自己缺失却尚未查明的真相）
vocab_notes.note_zh: 源自美国前国防部长 Donald Rumsfeld 著名的认识论修辞，本期借“已知的未知”与“未知的未知”巧妙串联起两幕关于记忆空白与人生谜团的故事。
Country two-step 是北美乡村音乐场景中非常普及的双人社交舞，此处勾勒出加拿大北部小镇的日常家庭生活氛围。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 麻木机械地应付日常；处于自动驾驶状态
vocab_notes.note_zh: 借用航空自动驾驶概念的常见口语隐喻，生动形容人在遭受心理创伤或抑郁时灵魂抽离、仅靠惯性维持生活的状态。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 装聋作哑的“中立国瑞士”
vocab_notes.note_zh: 融合了谚语“非礼勿视”（see no evil）与永久中立国瑞士的文化代称，讽刺父母在家庭性侵裂痕面前逃避表态的伪中立姿态。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 独门秘诀；核心制胜法宝
vocab_notes.note_zh: 原指快餐汉堡里的秘制酱料，在美式口语中广泛引申为某人之所以脱颖而出、卓有成效的关键特质。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 心理咨询腔；滥用的心理学术语套话
vocab_notes.note_zh: 当代北美流行文化热词，多含贬义，指将“创伤”“披露”“疗愈”等心理治疗词汇工具化，用以包装自私行为或逃避道德责任。
地道英语习语，指把隐瞒已久的秘密、谎言或罪责彻底坦白出来。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 放鸽子；刻意爽约或无视某人
vocab_notes.note_zh: 美式日常口语高频短语，指不把既定约会或他人的期待当回事而随意缺席。

transcript.speaker: Ira Glass
transcript.en: A quick warning, there are curse words that are un-beeped in today's episode of the show. If you prefer a beeped version, you can find that at our website, thisamericanlife.org.
transcript.zh: 先做个提醒，今天的节目中包含未被消音的粗口脏话。如果你想收听经过消音处理的版本，请登录我们的官网 thisamericanlife.org。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: It's This American Life. I'm Aviva DeKornfeld, sitting in for Ira Glass. So there's this recording I heard a couple months ago. And when I heard it, I could not believe it existed. I'd never heard anything like it.
transcript.zh: 这里是 This American Life。我是 Aviva DeKornfeld，代班 Ira Glass。几个月前，我听到了一段录音。听到的时候，我简直不敢相信世上居然会有这种录音存在。我以前从未听过类似的东西。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: It was recorded at a hotel bar at the Vancouver Airport by this woman named Vienna Luke. She'd arranged to meet with this guy, Justin, who she hadn't seen in almost a decade.
transcript.zh: 那是温哥华机场一家酒店的酒吧里录下的，录音者名叫 Vienna Luke。她约了一个叫 Justin 的男人见面，两人已经有将近十年没见了。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: She's sitting at a table. She orders a tea, sipping it slowly while she waits for him to arrive. She's wired for sound.
transcript.zh: 她坐在桌子旁，点了一杯茶，一边小口抿着，一边等他来。她身上绑着窃听录音设备。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: Every so often I'm kind of glancing towards the toward the hostess desk is, and then I see Justin walk in across the restaurant, and he's asking the hostess where I'm sitting, or like, or he's saying like I'm meeting someone here.
transcript.zh: 我不时往迎宾台那边瞟一眼。接着我看到 Justin 走了进来，穿过餐厅，他向领位员询问我坐哪儿，或者是在说‘我和别人约在这儿碰头’之类的话。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: Oh, I think the guy is here. Dang, looks exactly the same.
transcript.zh: 噢，他人好像到了。该死，长得跟当年一模一样。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: And I say, "Dang, he looks exactly the same." Like he is exactly who he has always been. He has not changed, and he has no idea what's coming, because he doesn't know I'm different.
transcript.zh: 我心里暗骂：‘该死，他简直一点都没变。’他还是原来那个他，没有丝毫改变，而且他根本不知道接下来会面对什么，因为他不知道如今的我已经脱胎换骨了。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Vienna's got a hidden recorder in her purse sitting on the table, and another recorder hidden in her bra. There are three cops in plain clothes sitting at tables around her, and a bunch more upstairs in a hotel room.
transcript.zh: Vienna 把一支录音笔藏在桌上的手提包里，另一支则藏在文胸内。四周的桌子旁坐着三名便衣警察，楼上的酒店客房里还埋伏着好几个。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Justin spots Vienna, walks over to her table, and Vienna jumps right in with a nervous preamble.
transcript.zh: Justin 发现了 Vienna，朝她的桌子走过来。Vienna 开门见山，带着紧张的语气做了开场白。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: Okay. So, yeah, obviously haven't really wanted to do this for quite some time. And, but I actually have a notebook today, and I wrote notes because I want to make sure that I cover off everything that I want to.
transcript.zh: 好吧。那个……很显然，在很长一段时间里我都不是很想做这件事。不过，我今天其实带了个笔记本，上面记了笔记，因为我想确保把我想说的事情都过一遍。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: Phew, and we're going to take this at my pace. And--
transcript.zh: 呼，咱们就按我的节奏来聊。还有——

transcript.speaker: Justin
transcript.en: Can I just ask, before we start, are you recording this?
transcript.zh: 在我们开始之前，我能问一句吗，你在录音吗？

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: No.
transcript.zh: 没有。

transcript.speaker: Justin
transcript.en: It wouldn't matter to me, because I feel this is your conversation and you do with it whatever you want.
transcript.zh: 我其实无所谓的，因为我觉得这是你的谈话，你想怎么样都可以。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Vienna is secretly recording because she's pretty sure that, years ago, Justin assaulted her. But she doesn't know for sure. She has big gaps in her memory from that night.
transcript.zh: Vienna 在秘密录音，因为她几乎断定，多年前 Justin 侵犯了她。但她不敢百分之百肯定。那一晚她的记忆存在巨大的空白断层。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Memory gaps are pretty common in cases of sexual assault, which makes for a horrible situation, because the one person who could clear things up and tell you what happened, the person who assaulted you, is the least likely person to talk to you and tell you the truth.
transcript.zh: 在性侵案件中，记忆断层非常普遍，这造成了一种极其残酷的局面：因为那个唯一能帮你解开谜团、告诉你究竟发生了什么的人——也就是侵犯你的那个人——偏偏是全天下最不可能坐下来跟你谈、跟你说实话的人。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Because why would they? In Vienna's case, though, the man, Justin, actually agreed to sit down with her and talk about everything, to answer all of her questions in detail.
transcript.zh: 毕竟他们凭什么答应呢？但在 Vienna 这个案子里，那个叫 Justin 的男人竟然真的同意坐下来跟她谈，从头到尾回答她的所有问题，事无巨细。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: I think most of us walk around with blank spots in our lives, small ones, big ones. And a lot of the time, you just give up on trying to get answers, accepting that you're just going to wonder forever.
transcript.zh: 我想我们大多数人的生活里都带着空白和谜团，有的微不足道，有的重若千钧。很多时候，大家索性放弃了追寻答案，认命地接受自己这辈子只能在困惑中度过。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: So what's it like to actually get all the answers you spent so long wondering about? And where's that leave you? Most of our show today is going to be the story of this recording. It's really remarkable. Stay with us.
transcript.zh: 那么，如果你苦苦琢磨了这么久的疑问，真的全都得到了确切的答案，会是怎样一种体验？这又会把你带向何方？今天节目的绝大部分内容，都是围绕这盘录音展开的。这段对话非同寻常。请不要走开。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: It's This American Life. Act One, "Known Unknowns." So Vienna is at this hotel bar at the Vancouver Airport, wearing that hidden recorder.
transcript.zh: 这里是《This American Life》。Act One，“已知的未知”。此时 Vienna 正坐在温哥华机场的一家酒店酒吧里，身上带着那台隐藏式录音机。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: And just a heads up before we start, this story includes a bunch of explicit details and references to sexual assault.
transcript.zh: 在开始之前先提醒一下大家，本期故事包含不少露骨细节，并涉及性侵话题。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: The man in the recording, which we'll get to in a minute, his name is Justin. He's a father of four boys, a veterinarian, though he has a sort of finance guy look about him, close-cropped hair, symmetrical face, wouldn't look out of place in a Patagonia vest.
transcript.zh: 录音里的那个男人，我们马上就会听到，他叫 Justin。他是四个男孩的父亲，一名兽医，但他身上却有种金融男的气质——寸头、五官端正对称，穿一件巴塔哥尼亚背心也毫无违和感。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Vienna is a fitness instructor, a mom to two kids. She's warm and sensitive and loves an inspirational quote. She and Justin are actually related. Justin is Vienna's brother-in-law, her oldest sister Sunny's husband.
transcript.zh: Vienna 是一名健身教练，也是两个孩子的母亲。她热情细腻，特别喜欢看那些励志名言。她和 Justin 实际上是亲戚。Justin 是 Vienna 的姐夫，也是她大姐 Sunny 的丈夫。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: I met him when I was 10. And, yeah, he felt like an older brother. And I'd only had sisters. So having a brother was exciting. And I thought he was charming.
transcript.zh: 我认识他时才十岁。而且，是啊，感觉他就像个亲哥哥。我身边只有姐妹，所以有个哥哥特别令人兴奋。当时我觉得他挺有魅力的。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: I mean, he was very self-assured. And I I guess I thought that was cool.
transcript.zh: 我的意思是，他身上那股自信很足。我想我当时觉得那样挺酷的。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: For 14 years, Vienna has wanted to ask Justin about one night from when she was 20 and he was 31. She was living with Sunny and Justin up in their small, northern Canadian town where they'd moved after they got married.
transcript.zh: 整整十四年来，Vienna 都一直想找 Justin 问个清楚——关于她二十岁、他三十一岁时发生的那一晚。当时她借住在 Sunny 和 Justin 家，就在他们婚后搬去的加拿大北部小镇上。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: And one day, when Sunny was away, Justin asked Vienna—
transcript.zh: 有一天，趁着 Sunny 不在，Justin 问了 Vienna 一句——

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: "Oh, do you want to, like, get drunk, to experience what it's like to be drunk in a safe place?" Like that was the promise.
transcript.zh: “你想不想喝个烂醉，在一个安全的地方体验一下喝醉到底是什么感觉？”他当时就是这么保证的。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Which sounded reasonable to Vienna. She and her family were evangelical Christians. She went to church every Sunday. Justin was part of the leadership.
transcript.zh: 这在 Vienna 听来很合情理。她和家人都是福音派基督徒，她每个礼拜天都去教堂，而 Justin 还是教会的骨干。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: And she'd had friends in the church who'd gotten drunk for the first time under a similar arrangement. So Justin makes Vienna a few mixed drinks to try, a strawberry daiquiri, a pina colada, some kind of Kahlua thing.
transcript.zh: 教会里有些朋友也是在类似的安全照应下第一次尝试喝醉的。于是 Justin 给 Vienna 调了几款鸡尾酒尝鲜：草莓德基利、椰林飘香，还有某种加了甘露咖啡利口酒的饮品。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Exactly the kind of drinks you might make for an abstinent 20-year-old trying to develop a taste for booze.
transcript.zh: 简直就是一个二十岁滴酒不沾、刚开始学着尝酒滋味的人会喝的典型饮料。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: ...or would order for yourself if you were 20 and didn't like the taste of alcohol.
transcript.zh: 或者说，你要是才二十岁又受不了酒精味，准会给自己点的那种酒。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: He's got music playing, like country music, and after I had a couple sips, he was, like, dancing with me, like two-stepping with me. And I feel like already then I was starting to feel a little bit, like, woozy.
transcript.zh: 他放着音乐，好像是乡村音乐。我喝了几小口后，他就拉着我跳舞，跳那种双步舞。我感觉就在那个时候，我已经开始觉得有点晕晕乎乎了。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: And then I basically lose feeling in my legs and collapse on the ottoman. And I'm like, oh my goodness, if this is what it feels like to be drunk, this is rough. Like, why do people-- why do people do this?
transcript.zh: 紧接着我的双腿基本上就没知觉了，整个人瘫倒在脚凳上。我心里想：天呐，要是喝醉了就是这感觉，那也太难受了吧。大家为什么——为什么还要喝酒啊？

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Vienna passes out. A little while later, she comes to in her bedroom, which is in the basement. She has no clue how she got there from the living room upstairs.
transcript.zh: Vienna晕了过去。过了一会儿，她在地下室的卧室里醒了过来。她根本不知道自己是怎么从楼上的客厅到这里的。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: And she only has one more brief memory from the evening. Warning for the listeners, this next detail might be upsetting.
transcript.zh: 对那个夜晚，她只剩下最后一段短暂的记忆。在此提醒听众，接下来的细节可能会让人感到不适。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: The one moment Vienna woke up, she remembers having an out-of-body experience, looking down at herself, seeing Justin taking off her underwear.
transcript.zh: Vienna唯一醒来的那个瞬间，她记得自己有一种灵魂出窍的感觉，低头看着自己，看到Justin正在脱她的内裤。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: The next morning, Vienna wakes up with a stomachache and a bad feeling. She tells Justin that she's not sure exactly what happened, but that she thinks he should tell Sunny.
transcript.zh: 第二天早上，Vienna醒来时肚子疼，心里也笼罩着一种不祥的预感。她告诉Justin，自己记不清到底发生了什么，但觉得他应该告诉Sunny。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: He brushes her off, saying there's no need to tell her. It'll just trouble her. And besides, nothing happened anyway.
transcript.zh: 他对此不以为意，说没必要告诉她，说了只会让她平添烦恼。况且，本来就什么都没发生。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: I'm like, okay, yeah, that's what I've been trying to tell myself too, like as this memory comes back.
transcript.zh: 我当时就想：行吧，也是，这段记忆涌上来的时候，我也一直试图这么说服自己。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: You were, like, almost hoping for that answer to be like, okay, it's nothing, right? It's nothing.
transcript.zh: 你几乎是在期盼得到这样的回答，好让自己觉得：行，没事，对吧？什么都没发生。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: Yeah, it's nothing. I mean, even in the moment, I remember telling myself, he's taking off my underwear because, like, I must have vomited. I must have gotten, like--
transcript.zh: 对，什么都没发生。我是说，甚至在那个当下，我都记得自己在心里开脱：他脱我内裤是因为……我肯定是吐了，我肯定是弄脏了……

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Like it, this must be a brotherly, familial act.
transcript.zh: 觉得这肯定是一个哥哥出于家人的照料举动。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: Yeah. Like, oh, he's just-- he's just changing my clothes because I threw up on myself. So I'd say things like that to myself. And then I'd be like, but why would he have to change my underwear?
transcript.zh: 对。就觉得，哦，他只是——他只是帮我换衣服，因为我吐在自己身上了。我当时就会用这些话安慰自己。可转念我又会想：但他凭什么要换我的内裤啊？

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: So this night happens. And Vienna has to decide, does she tell her family? And if she does, what exactly is she even telling them if she doesn't know any of the details?
transcript.zh: 那一夜就这样过去了。Vienna不得不做出抉择：要不要告诉家人？可要是说，在自己对细节一无所知的情况下，她到底又能跟他们说些什么？

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Vienna's family is one that makes a point to spend a lot of time all together-- Vienna's parents, her two sisters, and her. Vienna is the baby.
transcript.zh: Vienna的家是一个特别看重全家团聚的家庭——她的父母、两个姐姐，还有她。Vienna是家里最小的孩子。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: She grew up particularly close with her oldest sister, Sunny, Justin's wife. Sunny is 10 years older than Vienna, so she was more like a second mom to her.
transcript.zh: 她从小跟大姐Sunny（也就是Justin的妻子）感情尤为深厚。Sunny比Vienna大十岁，对她来说更像是第二个妈妈。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Sunny would dote on her, read "Junie B. Jones" to her at night. She painted a mural of farm animals on her bedroom wall. When Vienna got older, they'd bake chocolate chip cookies together.
transcript.zh: Sunny对她呵护备至，晚上会给她读《Junie B. Jones》，还在她卧室墙上画过农场小动物的壁画。等Vienna长大些后，两人还会一起烤巧克力曲奇。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: But for months after that night, Vienna doesn't tell anyone about what happened. Until, at the end of a family visit,
transcript.zh: 但在那一晚之后的几个月里，Vienna对所发生的事守口如瓶，没跟任何人提起过。直到后来在一次家庭聚会结束时，

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Vienna's middle sister, Shaughnessy, notices Justin pull Vienna into this long hug. A hug that looked too intimate to her eye. So, Shaughnessy, being the loud, confrontational one in the family, corners Vienna and badgers the truth out of her.
transcript.zh: Vienna的二姐Shaughnessy注意到Justin把Vienna拉过去，抱了很久。在她看来，那个拥抱显得过于亲昵了。于是，性格火爆、直来直去的Shaughnessy把Vienna堵在角落，硬生生把真相逼问了出来。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Vienna stumbles through a partial explanation, saying Justin gave her alcohol, but she can't bring herself to mention the one thing she remembers about the night, about him taking off her underwear. But even without that detail, something about the way Vienna was talking, her body language, Shaughnessy thought Justin must have done something inappropriate.
transcript.zh: Vienna结结巴巴地只说了一部分，说Justin灌了她酒，但她实在说不出口那天晚上她唯一记得的事——他脱了她的内裤。不过，即便少了那个细节，从Vienna说话的语气和肢体语言里，Shaughnessy还是断定，Justin肯定干了什么出格的事。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: So she convinces Vienna to tell their parents, and Vienna tells them what she told Shaughnessy. Vienna's parents are very surprised she got drunk. Vienna's dad calls Justin to get answers about what exactly happened. Justin, of course, downplays everything, saying Vienna just drank too much, that's all.
transcript.zh: 于是她说服Vienna告诉父母，Vienna就把跟Shaughnessy讲的那套告诉了父母。父母对她喝醉感到非常震惊。Vienna的父亲给Justin打电话，想问清楚到底发生了什么。当然，Justin把事情描得轻描淡写，说Vienna只是喝多了，仅此而已。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: When Justin's wife, Sunny, hears about all this, she shuts down entirely. Sunny's not her real name, by the way.
transcript.zh: 当Justin的妻子Sunny听说这一切时，整个人彻底封闭了。顺便提一下，Sunny并不是她的真名。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: My sister didn't want to know anything, and like, basically pretended like it didn't happen. I think everyone was just so confused. They didn't know what to do with it.
transcript.zh: 我姐姐什么都不想知道，基本上就假装这事从来没发生过。我觉得大家当时都懵了，不知道该怎么处理。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: And at the end of the day, people just, like they just want the family to be together. So pretty much it was just like life as usual after that. And I would have had to see him at the next family thing.
transcript.zh: 到头来，大家只是……他们只是希望一家人能整整齐齐的。所以基本上，在那之后日子就照旧过了。到了下一次家庭聚会，我又不得不面对他。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: There's a terrible ordinariness to sexual violence. I don't know any woman who hasn't, at some point, wondered if a man was going to hurt her. What's extraordinary about Vienna's story, though, is how she chose to respond to what happened to her.
transcript.zh: 性暴力有一种可怕的普遍性。我认识的女性里，几乎没有谁未曾某一刻担心过自己会不会被男人伤害。然而，Vienna的故事之所以与众不同，在于她最终选择如何回应降临在自己身上的伤害。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: But that doesn't happen for years, because for almost a decade, Vienna tried to continue on like normal. She's naturally a peacemaker, and pushing the issue with Justin just seemed like it would cause problems for everyone.
transcript.zh: 但这并不是立刻发生的，因为在将近十年的时间里，Vienna都试图若无其事地生活。她生来就是个和事佬，觉得紧咬着Justin不放只会给大家找麻烦。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Plus, at this point, Vienna is depressed, operating on autopilot, and didn't have the wherewithal to force her family to confront a thing she wasn't ready to deal with herself. So, instead, she went to university, spent time with her family, tried to figure out what she wanted to do with her life.
transcript.zh: 况且，那时的Vienna抑郁缠身，整个人全凭本能机械地活着，根本没有心力逼家人去直面一件连她自己都还没准备好面对的事。所以，她照常去上大学，陪伴家人，努力摸索自己的人生方向。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: But she couldn't shake the unsettled feeling she'd had ever since the night Justin gave her alcohol. And eventually, the uncertainty about what happened to her that night became this kind of torture, just question marks looping non-stop in the back of her brain as she went about daily life.
transcript.zh: 但自从Justin给她倒酒的那晚之后，那股不安的感觉就如影随形，挥之不去。久而久之，对当晚遭遇的茫然未解变成了一种折磨，在她过着日常生活的同时，无数个问号在脑海深处永无止境地盘旋打转。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Then, in 2014, seven years after the night Justin assaulted her, Vienna's oldest sister, Sunny, discovered that Justin was having an affair. Multiple affairs, actually. This news rocked their community.
transcript.zh: 后来，到了2014年——也就是Justin侵犯她整整七年后——Vienna的大姐Sunny发现Justin出轨了。事实上，是出轨了多个人。这个消息在他们的圈子里掀起了轩然大波。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Everyone had seen him as this wholesome family man, an elder in the church. Sunny ended up taking...
transcript.zh: 之前大家都把他看作顾家的好男人，还是教会里的长老。Sunny最终决定……

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Justin back after a couple of months. But for Vienna--
transcript.zh: 几个月后让 Justin 回到了家里。但对 Vienna 来说——

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: It was this affirmation that he was capable of not being a nice guy. I finally like believed myself.
transcript.zh: 这成了一种证实，证明他骨子里绝不是什么好人。我终于……开始相信自己的判断了。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: And what was it exactly that you believed?
transcript.zh: 那你具体相信了什么？

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: That he had done something to me, that something had happened.
transcript.zh: 相信他确实对我动过手脚，那一晚绝对发生了什么事。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: So Vienna cut Justin out. Shaughnessy did as well. She'd always believed Justin had done something to Vienna, even though at this point, Vienna still hadn't told her the detail about the underwear. Both refused to be in the same room as Justin.
transcript.zh: 于是 Vienna 与 Justin 断绝了往来。Shaughnessy 也同样如此。她一直坚信 Justin 伤害过 Vienna，尽管此时，Vienna 仍未把关于内裤的细节告诉她。姐妹俩都拒绝与 Justin 同处一室。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Vienna's parents positioned themselves as a kind of 'see no evil' Switzerland in the middle of this newfound estrangement, with Vienna and Shaughnessy on one side, and Justin and Sunny on the other. They felt uneasy about what they knew, but they didn't know how else to handle it.
transcript.zh: 面对这突如其来的隔阂，Vienna 的父母选择像“看不见邪恶”的中立国瑞士一样作壁上观：一边站着 Vienna 和 Shaughnessy，另一边是 Justin 和 Sunny。父母对所知道的情况隐隐感到不安，但他们不知道该如何处理。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: And so the entire family structure was reorganized to accommodate this vague, undiscussed thing that happened. For a family that loves spending time together, this meant no more holidays, no more family vacations. They all settled into a painful, awkward, strange new normal for a few years.
transcript.zh: 就这样，整个家庭的相处模式都被重构，以容纳这件模糊隐晦、心照不宣发生过的事。对于一个原本热衷于聚在一起的家庭来说，这意味着节假日泡汤，家庭度假取消。几年里，大家都困在了一种令人痛苦、尴尬而古怪的“新常态”中。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Until one night, Vienna called her middle sister, Shaughnessy, and said, 'I'm finally ready to figure out what happened to me.' It had been 12 years since the night.
transcript.zh: 直到某个深夜，Vienna 打电话给二姐 Shaughnessy 说：“我终于做好准备，去查明我身上到底发生过什么了。”距那个夜晚，已经过去了整整十二年。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: In order to go to the police, Vienna and Shaughnessy figured they need more evidence than Vienna's one memory of the night. So together, they make a list of everyone they knew Justin had been close with at the time of the assault, but wasn't close to anymore-- old coworkers, former friends. They figured maybe he had talked to someone about what he'd done.
transcript.zh: 要想报警，Vienna 和 Shaughnessy 清楚，单凭 Vienna 对当晚仅存的那点记忆，证据远远不够。于是她们联手列了一份名单，把所有在案发时与 Justin 走得很近、但如今已断了联系的人都记了下来——包括以前的同事、昔日的朋友。她们琢磨着，或许他曾对谁说漏嘴提起过自己的所作所为。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Vienna didn't want to talk to any of these people herself, so Shaughnessy calls roughly a dozen people, including one of Justin's former employees at the vet clinic he ran.
transcript.zh: Vienna 自己不想出面去接触这些人中的任何一个，于是 Shaughnessy 给大约十几个人打了电话，其中包括 Justin 曾经开办的宠物诊所的一名前雇员。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: And she says, 'I know why you're calling. He drugged your sister.' And continues to tell my sister everything she-- like, what she knows, that they were working in the back one day, um, in the clinic. And he says, like, 'If you were giving whatever drug it was to a human, how much would you give them to make sure they were out?'
transcript.zh: 那人直接说：‘我知道你为什么打电话来。他给你妹妹下了药。’接着便把她所知道的一切全盘告诉了我姐姐。她说有一天，他们在诊所后屋干活。他突然问：‘如果要给一个人喂某种药（不管是哪种），得下多大剂量才能确保对方完全昏死过去？’

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Another former employee told Shaughnessy that one day, the receptionist at the clinic was looking for something on the work computer and accidentally came across pictures of Justin with a naked woman who may have been Vienna. The woman's face wasn't visible. Some of the pictures were selfies Justin took, leaning against the woman's body.
transcript.zh: 另一名前雇员则告诉 Shaughnessy，有一天，诊所的前台在工作电脑上找文件，无意间翻到了 Justin 与一名赤裸女子的合照，那女子很可能就是 Vienna。照片里女人的脸看不清。其中有几张是 Justin 拍的自拍，整个人斜靠在那具女人的躯体上。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: With those two pieces of information about the drugs and the pictures, Vienna and Shaughnessy go to the police. Most--
transcript.zh: 握着这两条关键线索——迷药的传闻与电脑里的照片，Vienna 和 Shaughnessy 走向了警局。大多数……

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Sexual assault allegations that get reported, they never go anywhere. But Vienna gets extraordinarily lucky by getting the ear of a cop named Joelle Lachance, who's made tricky sexual assault cases her life's work.
transcript.zh: 很多被报案的性侵指控，最终都石沉大海。但 Vienna 却极其幸运，因为她遇上了一位名叫 Joelle Lachance 的警官，这位警官毕生都在攻克复杂的性侵案件。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: She's like one of those cops on a TV show whose secret sauce comes down to, she just really gives a shit. She used her vacation days to fly places for this case.
transcript.zh: 她就像电视剧里那种警察，破案的秘诀说到底就一条——她是真的把案子放在心上。为了这个案子，她甚至搭上了自己的年假自费坐飞机到处跑。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: She was late to her own sister's funeral because she was helping set up Vienna's Vancouver recording. The idea of going to the police more than a decade after an assault with only one memory of what happened and hearsay from a couple former acquaintances, and being taken seriously seems unimaginable.
transcript.zh: 她连自己亲妹妹的葬礼都迟到了，因为当时她正忙着帮 Vienna 筹划温哥华的那场录音。在一场侵害发生十多年后才去报警，手里仅有一段模糊的记忆和几个旧相识的传言，这种情况下居然还能被警方重视，简直让人难以置信。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: But that is what happened. Joelle ropes the undercover police team in to work with Vienna on her case. And they come up with a plan.
transcript.zh: 但事实就是如此。Joelle 把便衣卧底警察团队拉了进来，协助 Vienna 处理案子。他们一起制定了一个方案。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: For years, since Vienna first distanced herself from Justin, he had been emailing her periodically, asking her to return to the family. Vienna never responded to those emails.
transcript.zh: 这些年里，自从 Vienna 开始与 Justin 保持距离，他就经常隔三差五给她发邮件，求她回归家庭。Vienna 从来没有回过这些邮件。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: But now, with the help of the police, she crafted a response saying, basically, 'I'm willing to move past this, but in order for me to do that, I need you to tell me what happened that night.'
transcript.zh: 但这一次，在警方的指导下，她精心起草了一封回信，大意是说：“我愿意把这事翻篇，但前提是，你必须亲口告诉我那天晚上到底发生了什么。”

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Justin writes back and says, very clearly, that he sexually assaulted her. Vienna thinks, 'Okay, that was easy. We got him.'
transcript.zh: Justin 回信了，白纸黑字写得清清楚楚：他确实性侵了她。Vienna 当时心想：“行啊，这也太容易了吧。抓到他的把柄了。”

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: But the police say they need more concrete evidence, something undeniable. A lawyer in court could argue that someone other than Justin had written that email to Vienna.
transcript.zh: 但警方表示，他们需要更铁证如山的证据，必须无可辩驳。因为在法庭上，辩护律师完全可以辩称这封邮件根本不是 Justin 本人写的。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: And they needed specifics about what exactly he did. So Vienna writes Justin again, saying, 'We need to meet in person, and you need to tell me the details of what happened. That's the only way I'll be able to move forward.'
transcript.zh: 而且，他们需要弄清他具体做了什么的细节。于是 Vienna 再次给 Justin 写信，说：“我们得见一面，你必须当面告诉我当时的细节。只有这样，我才能彻底放下过去。”

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Justin, miraculously, agrees. Vienna thinks it's because he figured he would get to be the hero if he could be the one to reunite the family.
transcript.zh: 奇迹般地，Justin 答应了。Vienna 觉得，这是因为他自以为只要能促成家庭团聚，自己就能成为拯救一切的“大英雄”。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Justin offers to fly to Vancouver, where Vienna lives, so they decide to meet at the airport. The cops picked the airport because, even though they figured Justin wasn't likely an active threat to Vienna, they knew that if he had just walked off an airplane, there was no way he could have a weapon on him.
transcript.zh: Justin 主动提出飞到 Vienna 居住的温哥华，于是他们把见面地点定在了机场。警方之所以选在机场，是因为他们推断 Justin 应该不会对 Vienna 构成即时的人身威胁，而且刚下飞机的乘客绝不可能随身携带武器。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: And Vienna liked the airport idea, too. It felt comfortingly anonymous. In preparation for the meeting, the lead undercover cop spent a couple days training Vienna on how to get usable information out of Justin.
transcript.zh: Vienna 也很赞成在机场见面。那种人来人往的环境带有一种令人安心的匿名感。为了准备这次会面，卧底行动的带头警官花了几天时间对 Vienna 进行专项培训，教她如何从 Justin 口中套出法庭可采信的有效口供。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: So the day I did training, I brought in my notebook, and he was like, 'Whoa, this is so weird. You have a notebook? Like nobody brings a notebook.' Because usually—
transcript.zh: 去培训的那天，我带了个笔记本。他当时就愣了：“哇，这太稀奇了。你居然还带了笔记本？从来没人会带笔记本来的。”因为通常——

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Wait, why not?
transcript.zh: 等一下，为什么不带？

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: Because usually, he's like working with— um, he's like, 'You are very different than the undercover people I usually work with.' Which, not to like stereotype, but many of them were like criminals that he's like—
transcript.zh: 因为平时他接触的那些……他说：“你跟我平时合作的那些卧底线人简直天差地别。”倒不是我有意刻板印象，但他平时接触的很多都是罪犯，那些被他……

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Like he's flipped them, and then they're—

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: actually overruled the original sentence, and Justin had to serve out his term in federal prison. Though after just six months in prison, Justin was granted parole. Whatever you think of his sentence, this result is exceptionally rare.
transcript.zh: 推翻了原先的判决，Justin 必须去联邦监狱服刑。不过，在监狱待了区区六个月后，Justin 就获得了假释。不论你怎么看待他的量刑，这样的结果都极其罕见。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: The vast majority of sexual assaults are, of course, never reported to the police. And in Canada, of the cases that are reported and make it to court, only about 6% result in jail time for the perpetrator. So those are the sort of satisfying legal consequences.
transcript.zh: 绝大多数性侵案件当然根本不会向警方报案。而在加拿大，报案且走到起诉庭审阶段的案件中，只有大约6%会导致施害者入狱服刑。所以，从法律后果来看，这算得上差强人意了。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: But remember, Vienna went into this because ever since Justin assaulted her, she'd had this unsettled feeling, this itch to know what happened to her. And now that she knows, Vienna says that for the first time since that night, she's able to not think about what happened to her. She used to think about it all the time.
transcript.zh: 但别忘了，Vienna 最初之所以做这一切，是因为自从被 Justin 侵犯后，她心里一直悬着、像有根刺一样，非要弄清楚那晚到底发生了什么。如今她全知道了。Vienna 说，自那晚以来，她第一次可以不再去想发生在她身上的事了。过去她几乎无时无刻不在琢磨。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: It's kind of crazy how captive I was to everything that was done to me, the not knowing, and how much it, yeah, dictated so much of my life. And now, I don't have to worry about it anymore. I'm tired, and I'm just going to let the rest like, be.
transcript.zh: 想想还挺不可思议的，我之前居然被遭遇的那一切彻底囚禁住了，那种未知，那种……是的，它掌控了我生活的大部分。而现在，我再也不用为此担惊受怕了。我累了，接下来的事，就随它去吧。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: And then there's the last thing Vienna was hoping to get out of all of this. In some ways, it was the thing she wanted most, and that's getting her sister, Sunny, back. After the trial, once Vienna's parents learned the full extent of what Justin did to her, they cut Justin out.
transcript.zh: 此外，还有 Vienna 曾希望从这整件事中得到的最后一样东西。在某种程度上，那是她最渴望的——那就是挽回她的姐姐 Sunny。审判之后，一旦 Vienna 的父母得知了 Justin 对她所作所为的全部真相，他们就跟 Justin 断绝了往来。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: But Sunny is still married to him. Vienna had thought that if she could get Justin to lay out exactly what he did to her with all the graphic details, and if Sunny could hear that version of the story...
transcript.zh: 但 Sunny 依然维系着跟他的婚姻。Vienna 原本以为，如果自己能让 Justin 和盘托出所有的不堪细节、亲口讲出他是怎么侵犯她的，而 Sunny 也能听到这个版本的故事……

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: My hope is that she would be able to empathize, be able to be my sister instead of being his wife. I thought if she knew the truth, it would change everything.
transcript.zh: 我原本希望能唤起她的同理心，希望她能做回我的姐姐，而不是做他的妻子。我以为只要她知道了真相，一切都会改变。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: But as far as Vienna knows, Sunny never heard the tape. She served as a witness for Justin in the trial, and so was kept out of the courtroom until it was her time to be called to the stand, which meant she missed all the wiretape that Vienna's lawyers played in court. I reached out to Sunny and Justin multiple times and never heard back.
transcript.zh: 但据 Vienna 所知，Sunny 从没听过那盘录音。她在庭审中担任 Justin 的辩方证人，因此在被传唤出庭作证之前，一直被隔离在法庭之外，这意味着她错过了 Vienna 的律师在庭上播放的所有窃听录音。我曾多次联系 Sunny 和 Justin，但从未收到回复。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: It must be frustrating to do such a good job at getting the facts of what happened that night, and then for the facts to do nothing to persuade the person you're trying to convince the most that something did happen.
transcript.zh: 费了这么大劲把那晚的真相查得一清二楚，结果这些事实却丝毫说服不了你最想说服的人相信事情确实发生过，这一定让人很受挫吧。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: Yeah. Yeah, it's really, it's, it's really hard in terms of, you know, "Look at, look at, I did this for you, and you don't want to see it." Um, but I also, I mean, I can't have a relationship
transcript.zh: 是的。是啊，真的很……真的很难受，心想，“你看啊，你看，我这都是为了你做的，可你却偏偏不愿睁眼看。”嗯，但我也不……我的意思是，我没法维持这样一段关系……

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: If she can't recognize what happened, or what was done to me, like it's- it's- I, of course, I want a relationship with my sister. I love her deeply, but I also, I'm not okay with her staying married to him.
transcript.zh: 如果她不能承认发生了什么，不能承认我所受到的伤害，那……当然，我很想和我姐姐保持联系。我深深爱着她，但我也无法接受她继续和那个男人维持婚姻。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Yeah. They would need to break up in order for you to have a meaningfully close relationship with her again.
transcript.zh: 是的。要想重新恢复真正亲密的关系，他们俩必须得分开。

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: Yes.
transcript.zh: 对。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Do you hold out any hope of that happening?
transcript.zh: 你对这一天的到来还抱有希望吗？

transcript.speaker: Vienna Luke
transcript.en: Um, yeah. Like as much as I need to like move on and find peace, um, I always hold on to a little bit of hope.
transcript.zh: 嗯，有的。尽管我必须向前看、寻找内心的平静，但我心里始终保留着一丝希望。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: After Vienna's conversation with Justin, she drove home, exhaustion taking over as the adrenaline started to recede. She still had the goody bag from Sunny.
transcript.zh: 和 Justin 谈完后，Vienna 开车回了家。随着肾上腺素逐渐消退，巨大的疲惫感席卷而来。她手里还拿着 Sunny 给她的那个小礼袋。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Vienna's partner, Jordan, thought she should get rid of it, throw the stuff away. But she didn't want to. She used to love baking cookies with Sunny.
transcript.zh: Vienna 的伴侣 Jordan 觉得她应该扔掉它，把里面的东西通通处理掉。但她不想扔。她过去最喜欢和 Sunny 一起烤饼干了。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Maybe this was Sunny's oblique way of saying, "I know everything is messed up. I know I chose Justin over you. I know things won't ever be the same. But I'm still here, and I still love you."
transcript.zh: 也许这是 Sunny 一种隐晦的表达：“我知道一切都被搞得一团糟。我知道我选了 Justin 没选你。我知道再也回不到从前了。但我依然在，我也依然爱你。”

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: That's what Vienna would like to believe, anyway. So she unwrapped the cookies and ate them.
transcript.zh: 至少 Vienna 宁愿去这样相信。于是，她拆开包装，吃掉了那些饼干。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: This story first came to us from the CBC. They made a whole four-part series about Vienna, called "Personally: Agent Layla." Their story goes far beyond the tape you heard today.
transcript.zh: 这个故事最初来自加拿大广播公司（CBC）。他们围绕 Vienna 制作了一部四集系列节目，名为《Personally: Agent Layla》。他们讲述的细节远比大家今天听到的录音更丰富。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: There's a link to their series on our website. So go take a listen. If you've experienced sexual assault and want to talk to somebody, you can reach out to the National Sexual Assault Hotline, 1-800-656-HOPE.
transcript.zh: 我们的官网上有该节目的链接，欢迎大家去听听。如果你曾遭受过性侵犯并希望找人倾诉，可以拨打全美性侵救援热线：1-800-656-HOPE。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Coming up, a person passes a test they had no idea they were taking. That's in a minute, from Chicago Public Radio, when our program continues.
transcript.zh: 稍后，有人通过了一场自己完全不知情的测试。一分钟后请继续收听来自 Chicago Public Radio 的节目。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: It's This American Life. I'm Aviva DeKornfeld, sitting in for Ira Glass. Today's show, "The Missing Minutes."
transcript.zh: 欢迎收听《This American Life》。我是 Aviva DeKornfeld，代班 Ira Glass。今天的节目主题是《遗落的时光》。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: We've arrived at Act Two of our show. Act Two, Unknown Unknowns.
transcript.zh: 接下来进入节目的 Act Two。Act Two：未知的未知。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: So there's information you know you don't know, but then there's all the other stuff. Stuff that just doesn't quite make sense, but you don't know why. You feel like you're missing something.
transcript.zh: 世上有些信息，是你明知道自己不了解的；但还有另一类事情——那些说不清哪里不对劲、却又不知道缘由的事。你总觉得漏掉了关键拼图。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: So you hope that one day it'll all be explained and finally made clear. This last story is a short piece of fiction about what that day might be like. It's by Miranda July. Here she is.
transcript.zh: 于是你盼望着有朝一日，一切都能得到解答，真相大白。我们最后的这个故事是一则虚构短篇，描绘了真相揭晓的那一天可能会是怎样。作者是 Miranda July。请听她带来的朗读。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: Getting excited. Somebody somewhere is shaking with excitement because something tremendous is about to happen to this person.
transcript.zh: 兴奋正在蔓延。不知道在哪里的某个人，正因为激动而浑身发颤，因为一件极其了不得的大事即将降临在TA身上。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: This person has dressed for the occasion. This person's hoped and dreamed. And now it is really happening, and this person can hardly believe it.
transcript.zh: TA为这一刻盛装打扮。TA曾满怀期盼、做过无数次梦。而现在，一切真的在发生，TA甚至不敢相信。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: But believing is not an issue here. It is really, really happening.
transcript.zh: 但这已经无关相不相信了。因为这确确实实、真真切切地在发生着。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: It involves stepping forward and bowing. Possibly, there is some kneeling, such as when one is knighted. One is almost never knighted.
transcript.zh: 这需要TA向前迈步、鞠躬致意。可能还要单膝下跪，就像被册封为骑士那样。虽然现实中几乎没人会被封为骑士。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: But this person may kneel and receive a tap on each shoulder with a sword. Or, more likely, this person will be in a car, or a store, or under a vinyl canopy when it happens.
transcript.zh: 但这个人也许真会跪下，感受剑身在两肩各轻点一下。或者更可能的是，发生这事的时候，TA正坐在车里、身处便利店，或是躲在塑料雨棚下。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: Or online, or on the phone. It could be an email, "re: your knighthood," or a long, laughing, rambling phone message in which every person this person has ever known is talking on a speakerphone, and they are all saying, "You have passed the test.
transcript.zh: 也可能是在网上，或在通话中。可能是一封邮件，标题写着“关于您的骑士封号”；又或是一通很长、笑声不断、东拉西扯的电话留言，里面TA认识的所有人正开着免提，齐声说道：“你通过测试了。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: It was all just a test. We were only kidding. Real life is so much better than that."
transcript.zh: 那一切都只是一场测试。我们开玩笑的。真实的生活比那好太多了。”

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: This person is laughing out loud with relief and playing the message back to get the address of the place where every person this person has ever known is waiting to hug this person and bring her into the fold of life. It is really exciting, and it's not just a dream. It's real.
transcript.zh: 这个人如释重负地大笑出声，倒回去重放那条留言，想要听清集合地址——在那里，TA此生认识的所有人都正等待着拥抱TA，将她迎入生活的温暖怀抱。这实在太令人激动了，而且这绝不是一场梦。它是真的。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: They're all waiting by a picnic table in a park this person has driven past many times before. There they are. It's everyone.
transcript.zh: 他们全都在公园的一张野餐桌旁等候，而这个人以前曾无数次开车路过那座公园。他们就在那儿。所有人都在。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: There are balloons taped to the benches, and the girl this person used to stand next to at the bus stop is waving a streamer. Everyone is smiling.
transcript.zh: 长椅上用胶带绑着气球，曾经在公交站总站在TA身旁的那个女孩正挥舞着彩带。每个人脸上都洋溢着笑容。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: For a moment, this person is almost creeped out by the scene. But it would be so like this person to become depressed on the happiest day ever. So this person bucks up and joins the crowd.
transcript.zh: 有那么一瞬间，这幅景象几乎让TA有点毛骨悚然。但如果在这有生以来最幸福的一天突然消沉下去，那也太像TA的作风了。于是这个人振作起来，走进了人群之中。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: Teachers of subjects that this person wasn't even good at are kissing this person and renouncing the very subjects they taught. Math teachers are saying that math was just a funny way of saying, "I love you." But now they are simply saying it, "I love you."
transcript.zh: TA甚至根本不擅长的那些科目的老师，正亲吻着TA，并当场宣布放弃自己教过的那门课。数学老师们说，以前教数学只是用一种滑稽的方式来表达“我爱你”。但现在他们直接坦白了，“我爱你”。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: And the chemistry and PE teachers are also saying it. And this person can tell they really mean it. It's totally amazing.
transcript.zh: 化学老师和体育老师也这么说着。这个人能听得出，他们全都是发自真心的。这简直太不可思议了。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: Certain jerks and idiots and assholes appear from time to time, and it's as if they've had plastic surgery. Their faces are disfigured with love.
transcript.zh: 从前那些混球、白痴和讨厌鬼时不时冒出来，一个个就像整了容似的。他们的脸都被爱意扭曲得变了形。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: The handsome assholes are plain and kind, and the ugly jerks are sweet, and they are folding this person's sweater and putting it somewhere where it won't get dirty. Best of all, every--
transcript.zh: 英俊的混蛋变得朴素善良，丑陋的讨厌鬼变得温和体贴，他们正叠好这个人的毛衣，小心翼翼地放到不会弄脏的地方。最棒的是，每一位——

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: Person this person has ever loved is there, even the ones who got away. They hold this person's hand and tell this person how hard it was to pretend to get mad and drive off and never come back.
transcript.zh: 这个人爱过的每一个人都在场，甚至是那些最终离开的人。他们牵着这个人的手，诉说当初假装发火、开车离去并再也不回来是有多么艰难。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: This person almost can't believe it. It seemed so real. This person's heart was broken and has healed and now this person hardly knows what to think.
transcript.zh: 这个人简直不敢相信。当时的一切显得那么真实。这个人的心曾碎过，如今又愈合了，现在这个人几乎不知道该作何感想。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: This person is almost mad. But everyone soothes this person. Everyone explains that it was absolutely necessary to know how strong this person was.
transcript.zh: 这个人差点要生气了。但大家都来安抚。每个人都解释说，这绝对是必要的，他们必须知道这个人到底有多坚强。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: Oh, look, there's the doctor who prescribed the medicine that made this person temporarily blind. And the man who paid this person $2,000 to have sex with him three times when this person was very broke.
transcript.zh: 哦，看，那个开错药导致这个人暂时失明的医生也在。还有在那个人穷困潦倒时，花两千美元让这个人陪睡了三次的男人也在。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: Both these men are in attendance. They seem to know each other. They both have little medals that they're pinning on this person.
transcript.zh: 这两个男人都出席了。他们似乎还互相认识。他们手里都拿着小奖章，正往这个人身上别。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: They are badges of great honor and strength. The badges sparkle in the sunlight, and everyone cheers.
transcript.zh: 那是代表巨大荣誉与坚韧的勋章。勋章在阳光下闪闪发光，众人都欢呼起来。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: This person suddenly feels the need to check her post office box. It is an old habit, and even if everything's going to be terrific from now on, this person still wants mail.
transcript.zh: 这个人突然觉得该去看看自己的邮政信箱了。这是个老习惯了，就算从今往后一切都会好得不得了，这个人还是想收信。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: This person says she'll be right back, and everyone this person has ever known says, fine, take your time.
transcript.zh: 这个人说去去就回，而这个人认识的每一个人都说：行，慢慢来，别着急。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: This person gets in her car and drives to the post office and opens the box, and there is nothing, even though it is Tuesday, which is a famously good day for mail.
transcript.zh: 这个人上了车，开到邮局打开信箱，里面空空如也，尽管今天是周二——众所周知周二向来是个收信的好日子。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: This person is so disappointed. This person gets back in the car, and having completely forgotten about the picnic, drives home and checks the voicemail, and there are no new messages, just the old one about passing the test and life being better.
transcript.zh: 这个人失望透顶。这个人回到车里，把野餐的事忘得一干二净，直接开车回家去查语音信箱。没有新留言，只有那条旧的，说着通过了测试、生活会变好。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: There are no emails, either, probably because everyone is at the picnic. This person can't seem to go back to the picnic.
transcript.zh: 也没有新邮件，大概是因为所有人都还在野餐聚会上。这个人似乎没法再回野餐会去了。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: This person realizes that staying home means blowing off everyone this person has ever known. But the desire to stay in is very strong.
transcript.zh: 这个人意识到，呆在家里就意味着放了这个人生平所认识的所有人的鸽子。但想足不出户的念头极其强烈。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: This person wants to run a bath and then read in bed. In the bathtub, this person pushes the bubbles around and listens to the sound of millions of them popping at once.
transcript.zh: 这个人想放水泡个澡，然后躺在床上看书。泡在浴缸里，这个人拨弄着身边的泡沫，听着成千上万个气泡同时破裂的噼啪声。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: This person pushes the bubbles onto their breasts and makes weird shapes with the foam. By now, everyone must have realized that this person is not coming back to the picnic.
transcript.zh: 这个人把泡泡抹在胸口，用泡沫堆出各种怪异的形状。这会儿，大家肯定都已经意识到这个人不会回野餐会了。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: Everyone was wrong. This person is not who they thought this person was.
transcript.zh: 大家都想错了。这个人根本就不是他们以为的那副模样。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: This person plunges underwater. This person can stay underwater for an impressively long time, but only in a bathtub. This person wonders if there will ever be an Olympic contest for holding your breath under
transcript.zh: 这个人一头扎进水里。这个人能在水下憋很久很久，久得令人惊叹，但仅限于在浴缸里。这个人琢磨着，奥运会不知会不会设一个项目，比谁能在——

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: bath water. If there were such a contest, this person would surely win it. An Olympic medal might redeem this person in the eyes of everyone this person has ever known.
transcript.zh: 浴缸水下憋气最久。如果有这样的比赛，这个人肯定能赢。一枚奥运奖牌或许能在这个人认识的所有人眼中挽回形象。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: But no such contest exists, so there will be no redeeming. This person mourns the fact that she has ruined her one chance to be loved by everyone.
transcript.zh: 但根本没有这种比赛，所以也不可能有什么救赎。这个人哀叹着自己毁掉了被所有人深爱的唯一机会。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: As this person climbs into bed, the weight of this tragedy seems to bear down upon this person's chest. And it is a comforting weight, almost human in heft.
transcript.zh: 当这个人爬上床时，那场悲剧的沉重感仿佛压在了胸口。那是一种令人安心的重量，几乎有着活人般的份量。

transcript.speaker: Miranda July
transcript.en: This person sighs. This person's eyes begin to close. This person sleeps.
transcript.zh: 这个人叹了口气。闭上双眼。这个人睡着了。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Miranda July, she's the author of the book, All Fours, which is the only book that I, upon completing, flipped over and immediately started reading again. I can't recommend it enough.
transcript.zh: 那是 Miranda July。她是小说《All Fours》的作者——这也是唯一一本我刚读完就立刻翻回第一页重读的书。怎么推荐都不为过。

transcript.speaker: Aviva DeKornfeld
transcript.en: Miranda also has a Substack called, appropriately, Miranda July. Check it out.
transcript.zh: Miranda 在 Substack 也有专栏，名字也很贴切，就叫《Miranda July》，大家不妨去看看。
